name: MindBridge Quorum Social Integration BCI
description:
The MindBridge Quorum is a consumer BCI engineered specifically around social connectivity, prioritizing low-latency group messaging, proximity social-feed integration, and real-time emotional-tone tagging over raw processing power. Its primary innovation is the Quorum Social Layer — a proprietary protocol that allows up to 200 simultaneous neural-linked contacts within a 50-meter radius, enabling the kind of rapid, layered social communication that defines Tier 2-3 community life: group alerts, shared AR spaces, split-second payment splitting, and neighborhood broadcast channels. The hardware footprint is smaller than most competitors, using a four-point subdural mesh rather than six, which reduces installation time to roughly 30 minutes.

The Quorum is enormously popular in the densely populated residential blocks of Tiers 2 and 3, where community life is organized through tight-knit neighborhood networks and the ability to broadcast quickly to trusted contacts is a genuine safety and social currency asset. Street vendors use it to coordinate pitch territory. Building co-ops use it to manage shared resource pools. Young people use it to build social graphs that function as informal credit and reputation systems. Critics note that the Quorum's social-graph data is sold to MindBridge's advertising partners under an opt-out model that most users never navigate, and privacy advocates have long called it the most aggressively monetized BCI on the mass market.
installation_requirements: Outpatient clinic or licensed installation kiosk; local anesthetic; 30-minute procedure; parental consent required for users under 16
rejection_risk: Minimal — four-point mesh uses flexible biofilm contacts with industry-leading 98.7% compatibility; designed for broad demographic tolerance
maintenance: Social-layer protocol updates weekly via passive background sync; hardware recalibration annually; social graph pruning recommended every 6 months to prevent contact-list bloat causing latency spikes
specifications: {"bandwidth": "3.1 Gbps neural throughput", "social_radius": "50m proximity network, 200 simultaneous contacts", "channels": "4 subdural mesh points", "encryption": "social-layer AES-128, civic-layer AES-256", "battery": "inductive charging, 22-hour active cycle", "latency": "8ms social-layer response, 15ms feed response", "storage": "1.5TB onboard cache", "connectivity": "MeshNet, civic ID, payment rail, social graph, neighborhood broadcast"}
side_effects: Social-feed saturation syndrome in high-density environments — users in crowded spaces report anxiety and difficulty filtering simultaneous contact pings
Mild empathy-bleed from emotional-tone tagging feature; some users report unconsciously mirroring the mood states of nearby contacts
Dependency formation — clinical studies show Quorum users exhibit measurable social anxiety when the unit is offline or out of range
Occasional contact-list ghost signals from deceased or deactivated users whose profiles persist in the social graph
cultural_context: The Quorum occupies an interesting social position — it is simultaneously the BCI most associated with community solidarity and the one most criticized by privacy advocates. In Tier 2 residential blocks, having a Quorum is almost a prerequisite for meaningful neighborhood participation; community alert networks, mutual aid groups, and informal credit circles all run on the Quorum's social layer. This creates a soft coercion dynamic: refusing to install one means social exclusion from networks that have real material consequences. The MindBridge corporation leans heavily into this community identity branding while quietly operating one of the most extensive behavioral data collection operations in Meridian 88.
known_users: Residential block community organizers and co-op managers
Street vendors and market traders who work in close proximity
Youth social networks and gang-adjacent community groups
Neighborhood watch and mutual aid collectives
Social media influencers working the Tier 2-3 content market
story_hooks: A neighborhood's Quorum broadcast network — used for everything from childcare alerts to emergency warnings — has been quietly hijacked. Someone with deep MindBridge backend access is inserting false alerts and selectively suppressing real ones. The players must trace the intrusion before a manufactured panic turns violent.

A deceased contact's ghost signal keeps appearing on a player's Quorum social graph — but the messages it sends contain information that the dead person couldn't have known while alive, referencing events that happened after their death.

MindBridge is rolling out a 'community wellness' update to the Quorum's emotional-tone tagging system — but leaked internal documents suggest the update is actually a large-scale mood manipulation trial, designed to test whether consumer BCIs can be used to suppress civil unrest in Tier 2 districts.
